Hey <@804012503406215258> - when I started with OpenClaw, memory basically meant "a daily log" period. So I started giving it specific instructions to create distinct files for people, places, companies, etc. and build knowledge that way. The new "memory wiki" plugin gives it some of this guidance automatically. So the first version of "muck around" is just structuring it beyond simple semantic retrieval based on how I commonly access it. More recently I'm studying how I actually ask questions about things and have more specific instructions for my OpenClaw about how to process ingest and store information to surface answers more quickly. For example, when I provide meeting transcripts, I don't just want the raw transcript and summary in memory; I want distinct characterizations of what was discussed, by whom, in what context, etc.

messages.content:
its a great question and i would have gotten to it, if we'd had more time.
my general advice is to experiment with different models and different tools to see what works for you.
and most of all avoid getting locked into any one tool!
i have used VSCode for years so like using different provider plugins there
i also love using the terminal so use claude code a bunch

having said that, as <@618851450273136651> mentioned at the start, on some days claude just feels really dumb so i need a back up plan! and like wes and many others, i often use claude models to build and codex to test.
don't get caught up in the twitter fueled model/harness/vendors wars (or at least if you do, know that's what's happening) -- find tools that work for you and don't get locked in
also semi pro tip: use smarter reasoning models  (eg opus) for planning and faster cheaper models (eg sonnet) for executing
more best practices and pro tips from the sharp af minds of <@751156367506800701> and <@736013353998090241> here https://hugobowne.substack.com/p/how-to-build-an-ai-agent-with-ai

I'm mostly using skills for connecting to services that are unique to me, most of them are custom and unique to me and my org or doing regualr task to my flavour. I also use cursor, alot of people say the editor is gone but its still there.  The changes in codex, e.g. the remote feature (this one i think is huge - I'm getting a old laptop back online for this) and how the apps improved. 

Elainer and her little antidotes about hermes, im a hermes user.  Im still figureing out why its useful.  Not using it for creating apps but for those not coding task, i cant remember which tips as i get alot of tips from her social media.
